title: Move zeros right while preserving nonzero order
answer: Use a write pointer that tracks the next position for a non-zero value. Scan the array from left to right; whenever a value is non-zero, copy it to `values[write]` and increment `write`. After all non-zero values have been compacted at the front, fill the remaining positions from `write` to the end with zeros. AeroTopo's `moveZerosRight` method does exactly this. It runs in O(n) time, uses O(1) extra space, modifies the array in place, and preserves the relative order of non-zero elements.
